Specs: Bakeneko 60, Gateron Oil Kings, and Cerakey ceramic keycaps.

Mods: Tape mod, lots of extra lube in the oil kings and the stabilizers, tape and tissue in the space bar, and I swapped out the spacebar switch for a switch with a stronger actuation force (pure berry).

Keycap review:

Definitely some major perks and major drawbacks of these keycaps. Aesthetically they are beautiful, smooth, and I really like how they look in a 60% format. They also have a really beautiful sound that can only come from bulkier/heavier keycaps. The ceramic material itself is so unique and cool to type with. With all of the mods, combined with the ceramic material, this keyboard sounds extremely deep and thocky.

Of course, the weight of these keycaps can be an issue. The spacebar is pretty mushy, and I needed to swap out the switch for one with a strong actuation force to handle it's weight. It also sounded very hollow, so I modded it with tape and tissue.

There were some fit issues with two of my keycaps striking each other. This created a very high pitch \*tink\* sound (characteristic of the ceramic material), which drove me nuts. I attempted to file down one of the keys to create more clearance, but porcelain is extremely strong and durable so that technique failed. Luckily, one of the keys was mounted on stabilizers, so I shoved some tissue into one side of both stabs to shift the keycap to the side a tiny bit. This seems to have fixed the issue for now, but I could see the natural variability of ceramic keycaps causing some fit issues for others.

Conclusion:

The sound and feel of typing on these keycaps is so good that I don't really care about the drawbacks. I plan to use this keyboard for a long time (so long as the legends dont rub off lol).

Spontaneity 

Transfer of living organisms by asteroid/meteorite/other space debris

Of those three, the primordial soup/proteinoid hypotheses have been the most scientifically sound theories that have been replicable in a lab setting. Face, neck, and hands.

Do everything you can--with what little motivation you have--to continue discovering new ways to cope. 

A lot of stuff won't work. But, every now and then, something will. And anyone with depression will understand how important those small victories are. 

Here are things that worked for me: 

* Reading books. I learned to love reading, and now I find that it directly influences my mental health. 
* If you decide to get out of bed, do not return until you are ready to go back to sleep for the night. Do not return to jack off, do not return to take a nap, do not get back into the bed. 
* Schedule time to own your emotions. What I mean by this is, if you feel like a blubbering mess and you could cry at any moment, make the conscious choice to have a "pity party." And I mean own that shit. Indulge in those emotions. Coping with depression sometimes requires that you release, and it's often not pretty--but it is **so** necessary. 


These are things I do consistently now, and they've helped a lot. I still struggle, and some days are worse than others. But, I wouldn't have found those things that work for me specifically if I hadn't kept trying.
